The app lives on a separate VM at 51.79.226.200, reachable via `ssh -i /root/.ssh/soulpilates_deploy root@51.79.226.200`. Prod tree: `/opt/soulpilates`. Staging tree: `/opt/soulpilates-staging` (public at staging.soulpilates.com.vn). Do NOT `git stash`, `git checkout --`, or `git reset` anything in either tree — those uncommitted changes are load-bearing for currently-running prod features, not junk.

Deploy mechanics (confirmed from a prior session's notes): the docker-compose frontend/backend services have only `image:`, no `build:`, so `docker compose up --build` is a no-op. To actually deploy a change: `docker build -t soulpilates/backend:{staging|latest} -f SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile .` (context = repo root) for backend, or `docker build -t soulpilates/frontend:{staging|latest} --build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=<url> -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile SoulPilates.Astro` for frontend, then `docker compose -f docker-compose.{staging|prod}.yml --env-file <env> up -d --force-recreate <service>`. ALWAYS build/deploy to STAGING first (`/opt/soulpilates-staging`, `docker-compose.staging.yml`), verify, and leave prod alone unless explicitly told to promote — the owner promotes to prod themselves after verifying.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: you must NOT write to the production MongoDB financial data (invoices, payments, ledger) under any circumstances — a prior session found this is blocked by a safety classifier anyway, and the owner's standing policy is that they run financial DB writes themselves after reviewing your diagnosis. You may run READ-ONLY mongo queries against prod to diagnose (e.g. via `docker exec` into the mongo container, or through the app's read APIs) but never inserts/updates/deletes on prod data. Staging's database, if it has test-only data, is fair game for testing your code fix against.

There are two things to do, both filed as cards on the owner's project board (already read and diagnosed at a high level — you're picking up mid-investigation):

## Task 1: Fix the Collect-flow discount bug (recurring)

Two weeks ago (2026-08-16) this exact bug was diagnosed: the studio "Collect" payment flow (`SchedulingService.CollectStudioPaymentAsync`, triggered by the front-desk "Collect" button) has **no discount field** — its request DTO only carries `ReferralDiscountPct`, and the invoice it creates hardcodes `TotalDiscount`/`LineDiscount` to `0m`. Only the separate manual `InvoiceController` path honors discounts. The fix was diagnosed but NEVER actually shipped as code — only two old invoices were manually patched at the DB level as a one-off. It just recurred: a new invoice, SP-INV-260826-0002 (client Alexandra Zehetmeier, "duet class", 2× Private Session @ 850,000 = 1,700,000đ total, PAID, Disc column blank), was supposed to get a −400,000đ discount at Collect time and it silently didn't apply.

Also investigate a second, related anomaly on this SAME invoice: 1,700,000đ = 850,000 × 2 (the OLD pre-fix duo math), but a private-duo flat-price fix was supposedly shipped 2026-08-16 (`GlobalSettings.PrivateDuoPrice` defaulting to 1,300,000, applied via `PaymentService.DuoAwareTotal(format, dropIn, seats, privateDuoPrice)` in `QuotePriceAsync` AND in `SchedulingService`'s desk-collect `expectedAmount`/no-show `newDue` paths) — and 1,700,000 − 400,000 = 1,300,000 exactly, suggesting the staff member tried to manually correct a duo-pricing miss with a discount that then failed to apply. Read `PaymentService.cs` and `SchedulingService.cs` (already has DuoAwareTotal per the uncommitted diff) and figure out why this specific booking/invoice ended up on the 2×850,000 path instead of the flat 1,300,000 duo path — e.g., was it created through a booking flow that doesn't call DuoAwareTotal at all (walk-in/manual invoice creation vs. the "Make it a Duo Class" checkbox flow)? Read-only diagnosis for this part — do not change duo-pricing logic unless it's trivially the same root cause as the discount fix.

**Your job**: actually implement the discount-field fix in code, on the staging tree (`/opt/soulpilates-staging`), on top of the existing uncommitted changes (don't disturb them). Add a `DiscountAmount` (or similarly-named) field to whatever request DTO backs the Collect flow, thread it through into the invoice creation so `TotalDiscount`/`LineDiscount` reflect it (the invoice/pricing service already recomputes totals elsewhere per prior notes — reuse that), and add the corresponding input control in the Collect modal on the frontend (Astro). Build and deploy to staging (following the manual docker build steps above), and verify end-to-end on staging using a test booking/invoice (create one on staging, use Collect with a discount, confirm the resulting invoice shows the discount and correct net total) — do not use prod data for this verification. Do NOT touch the real SP-INV-260826-0002 invoice or any other prod financial record — diagnosis only for that specific invoice; the owner will decide how to correct it (refund/credit) themselves.

## Task 2: "Nakko can't add attendee to a class that isn't hers"

A staff member named Nakko cannot add an attendee to a class she doesn't own/isn't the instructor for. This is presumably an overly-strict ownership/permission check somewhere in the class/booking attendee-add flow (likely a controller or service method checking `instructorId == currentUser.Id` or similar before allowing an attendee add). Find the relevant code (search the backend for attendee-add endpoints/methods — likely in a BookingController, SchedulingController, or ClassController, and the corresponding service layer), identify the exact check that's blocking her, and determine the *correct* intended behavior (front-desk/other instructors should very likely be able to add attendees to any class — that's normal studio front-desk behavior; a class being "not hers" shouldn't block admin/reception actions like this). Confirm your understanding by checking whether other staff/roles have this same restriction or if it's specific to non-owning instructors, and check what role Nakko has (query the staging or prod DB read-only for a user/staff record matching "Nakko" to see her role). Implement the fix on staging (loosen the check appropriately — e.g., allow any authenticated staff/instructor/admin role to add attendees, not just the class's assigned instructor, unless there's a legitimate reason for the restriction you should preserve, like a genuinely instructor-only class type), build, deploy to staging, and verify.

## Reporting

When both tasks are done (or if you get blocked), report back clearly: what was changed (files, the actual diff summary), what you verified on staging, the root cause you found for the duo-pricing anomaly on SP-INV-260826-0002 (even though you won't fix that specific invoice), Nakko's actual role/permission finding, and an explicit READY-FOR-PROD-PROMOTE checklist the owner can review before you (or they) push this to `/opt/soulpilates` prod. Do not deploy anything to prod yourself. If you hit the financial-DB-write classifier block or any other hard stop, report exactly what got blocked and what you need from the owner to proceed.

The fix needs to thread the discount amount through to `classBody` and into the backend's collect-payment request so the class portion also gets discounted correctly.

# Staging & release workflow — setup guide

This repo now supports a proper **staging → GitHub → production** flow so you
never develop directly on the live system again.

```
edit on a branch (staging dir)  →  deploy-staging + test
   →  push to GitHub  →  merge to main  →  deploy-prod
```

## What's already been set up
- **Full backup** taken before any changes → `/opt/backups/soulpilates-<timestamp>/`
  (`db-mongodump.archive.gz` + `full-soulpilates.tar.gz`, verified).
- **Git repo** initialized at `/opt/soulpilates` with a baseline commit; branches
  `main` (production) and `develop` (work). Secrets/data are gitignored.
- **Staging stack files**: `docker-compose.staging.yml`, `staging.env.sample`.
- **Scripts**: `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`, `scripts/deploy-prod.sh`,
  `scripts/sync-staging-db.sh`.

## One-time setup you need to do (needs your accounts / DNS)

### 1. Push the repo to GitHub
```bash
cd /opt/soulpilates
# create a PRIVATE repo on github.com first, then:
git remote add origin git@github.com:<you>/soulpilates-crm.git
git push -u origin main
git push origin develop
```

### 2. Create the staging working directory (separate from live)
Staging is a **second checkout** so editing/testing never touches the live source:
```bash
git clone /opt/soulpilates /opt/soulpilates-staging      # or clone from GitHub
cd /opt/soulpilates-staging
git checkout develop
cp staging.env.sample staging.env       # then fill in — see step 3
```

### 3. Fill in `staging.env` (own secrets, NOT prod's)
Generate fresh values so staging is fully isolated:
```bash
# JWT + passwords
openssl rand -hex 32          # → JWT_SECRET
openssl rand -hex 16          # → MONGO_PASSWORD / REDIS_PASSWORD / RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY
# VAPID keypair for web push (or reuse a throwaway pair)
```
Set `SMTP_TEST_REDIRECT_TO=` to your own inbox (test emails go there, never to
customers). Keep `STRIPE_ENABLED=false` unless testing payments with `sk_test_…`.

### 4. Point a staging subdomain at it (nginx + cert)
Add DNS `staging.soulpilates.com.vn` → this server, then an nginx server block
(mirror the prod one) with a TLS cert, proxying:
- `/api` and `/soulpilates-public` → the backend/rustfs (`127.0.0.1:8491`, `:6424`)
- everything else → the frontend (`127.0.0.1:3819`)

Recommended: protect the whole staging host with HTTP basic-auth so it isn't public.

### 5. Bring staging up + load data
```bash
cd /opt/soulpilates-staging
scripts/deploy-staging.sh develop     # builds :staging images, starts the stack
/opt/soulpilates/scripts/sync-staging-db.sh   # copies prod data in (PII scrubbed)
```

## Day-to-day workflow
1. In `/opt/soulpilates-staging`, branch off develop: `git checkout -b feature/x`.
2. Make changes there and `scripts/deploy-staging.sh feature/x` to test.
3. Commit + push: `git push origin feature/x`; open a PR into `main` on GitHub.
4. After review/merge, publish live: on **`/opt/soulpilates`** run
   `scripts/deploy-prod.sh` (pulls `main`, rebuilds, recreates the app containers).

> The live production dir (`/opt/soulpilates`) should only ever be updated via
> `deploy-prod.sh` (i.e. from merged `main`), not hand-edited.

## Restore from backup (if ever needed)
```bash
BK=/opt/backups/soulpilates-<timestamp>
# DB only:
docker exec -i soulpilates-prod-mongo sh -c 'mongorestore -u USER -p PASS \
  --authenticationDatabase admin --archive --gzip --drop' < "$BK/db-mongodump.archive.gz"
# Everything (code + configs + data): extract the full archive
tar xzf "$BK/full-soulpilates.tar.gz" -C /some/restore/path
```

Everything is deployed and stable. Here is my final report.

## Summary

### Task 1 — Collect-flow discount bug

**Root cause (confirmed by reading `ClassDetailPanel.astro`'s mini-POS code):** the Collect modal already has a discount input (`mposDiscAmt`/`mposDiscType`), and `mposRecalc()` correctly *displays* a discounted total to the staff member. But in `mposComplete()`, the discount was only ever forwarded to the separate `/api/invoice` call for **product/merch lines** (`prodDisc`). The class charge itself was sent as `{ amount: m.dropInPrice, ... }` — the full undiscounted price — to `/api/scheduling/booking/{id}/collect-payment`, which has **no discount field at all** in its DTO or in `SchedulingService.CollectStudioPaymentAsync`. For a class-only sale (no product lines, like the duet class), the discount the staff saw on screen was silently discarded and the full amount was charged. This exactly reproduces SP-INV-260826-0002.

**Fix implemented (staging: `/opt/soulpilates-staging`):**
- `SoulPilates.API/Controllers/SchedulingController.cs` — added `DiscountAmount` to `CollectBookingPaymentRequest`, threaded into the service call.
- `SoulPilates.Core/Interfaces/ISchedulingService.cs` / `SoulPilates.Services/SchedulingService.cs` — `CollectStudioPaymentAsync` now takes `decimal? discountAmount = null`. `amount` stays the net collected amount; `grossAmount = amount + discount` is used for `UnitPrice`, and `TotalDiscount`/`LineDiscount` are set to the real discount (reusing `InvoiceService.CreateInvoiceAsync`'s existing total/line-total recompute, as hinted). A discount now requires a `notes` reason, same bar as any other custom-amount deviation. The pre-existing `existingInvoice` (partial/Stripe-deposit) branch is explicitly left alone with a comment — discounting a balance top-up on an already-created invoice was out of scope.
- `SoulPilates.Astro/src/components/admin/ClassDetailPanel.astro` — added `_mposClassAmounts()` helper; `mposComplete()` now sends `discountAmount` and the *net* amount for the class charge; `_mposBills()` (tender/split validation) updated to match so split payments reconcile with a discount applied.

**Duo-pricing anomaly on SP-INV-260826-0002 (read-only diagnosis, not fixed):** Read-only Mongo query on prod confirmed Attendance `Quantity=2`, session `Format="PRIVATE"`, `DropInPrice=850000`. The backend's `expectedAmount` calc in `CollectStudioPaymentAsync` *does* call `PaymentService.DuoAwareTotal` correctly. The bug is purely in the frontend mini-POS: `mposSetAttending()`/`showCollectPayment()` in `ClassDetailPanel.astro` compute the class amount as `perSeat * n` using the session's raw flat `dropInPrice`, entirely bypassing `DuoAwareTotal`/`GlobalSettings.PrivateDuoPrice`. So even though the 2026-08-16 duo fix landed in the backend, the Collect modal never adopted it, so the front desk saw/charged 1,700,000 (2×850,000) instead of the flat 1,300,000. The note "duet class" satisfied the backend's mismatch-requires-a-note check, letting the wrong amount through. This is a distinct bug from the discount bug (not touched, per instructions — read-only diagnosis only).

### Task 2 — Nakko can't add attendee to a class that isn't hers

Nakko's actual Staff/User role is **`HeadInstructor`** (Staff.Name="Nakko", linked User email `nhi@soulpilates.com.vn`, confirmed via read-only Mongo query on both prod and staging).

**Root cause:** `InstructorController.cs` has an `IsHeadInstructor()` helper explicitly documented as granting a HeadInstructor "read access to EVERY instructor's classes... oversees the whole studio's schedule," and it's already used to bypass ownership checks on the *read* endpoints (class detail, waitlist) and the "all instructors" schedule view. But the *write* endpoint `AddStudentToMySession` (`POST session/{id}/add-student`) only bypassed the ownership check for `IsAdminRole()`, not `IsHeadInstructor()` — so a HeadInstructor got the exact same 403 ("You can only add clients to your own sessions") as a plain Instructor. This is inconsistent with how the rest of the app treats HeadInstructor (e.g. `SchedulingController` grants `Admin,Receptionist,HeadInstructor` equal roster-management rights everywhere).

**Fix implemented:** added `!IsHeadInstructor()` to the bypass condition in `AddStudentToMySession` and its sibling `RemoveMyAttendee` (the matching attendee-removal endpoint, same risk profile). Left the schedule-structure endpoints (cancel/reschedule-time/transfer-to-another-instructor, lines ~388/413/438/610) untouched — those alter another instructor's actual schedule/ownership rather than just the roster, which is a plausible legitimate reason to keep them owner-scoped, and none of that was reported broken.

Everything is deployed and healthy. Here's my report on both follow-up items.

## Item 1 — E2E verification: both PASS

Logged in successfully with `admin@soulpilates.com.vn` / `password`.

**1a. Collect-flow discount — PASS.** Created a test client + a 2-seat PRIVATE session/booking (850,000 × 2) on staging, then called Collect with `amount:1300000, discountAmount:400000`. Resulting invoice: `totalGross: 1,700,000`, `totalDiscount: 400,000`, `totalNet: 1,300,000`, `status: PAID`, roster shows `paymentStatus: paid`, `stillOwes: false` — exactly the outcome wanted for SP-INV-260826-0002.

While verifying I caught a **second, real bug my own fix exposed**: the attendance's post-collect `AmountDueAtStudio` recompute (`newAmountDue = AmountDueAtStudio - amount`) didn't know about the discount, so a fully-discount-settled booking was left showing a phantom 400,000 "still due" — which also gates the BOGO free-class credit grant (`if (newAmountDue <= 0)`), so a legitimately-fully-paid booking would have silently failed to grant its BOGO credit. Fixed in the same `SchedulingService.cs`: `newAmountDue` now subtracts `amount + discount` from the gross snapshot. Retested — `remainingDue: 0` in the response, confirmed correct.

**1b. HeadInstructor add-attendee — PASS, with a clean negative control.** I couldn't use Nakko's real account (no known password, and resetting it would require the same blocked DB-write/token-forging paths from before), so I created a throwaway `HeadInstructor` staff+login via the legitimate `POST /api/staff` + `POST /api/staff/{id}/login` admin APIs (no DB writes, no secret extraction) — same role as Nakko. That test account successfully added (200) and removed (200) an attendee on a class owned by a different instructor (Lavie) via the instructor-portal endpoints. As a control, a throwaway plain `Instructor` account got the expected `403 "You can only add clients to your own sessions."` on the same session — proving the fix is scoped correctly (HeadInstructor only, not a blanket loosening). All test sessions/staff were cleaned up afterward (sessions cancelled, test staff deactivated and logins unlinked).

## Item 2 — Cart-based POS discount bug: fixed

Read `pos.astro`'s `checkout()` fully. Confirmed the identical pattern: one combined `discAmount` computed for the whole cart, but only ever sent to `/api/invoice` for merch/package lines (`nonClassItems`) — `collectItems` (existing-booking collect-payment lines) got zero discount, and in a **mixed cart** the entire cart-wide discount was dumped onto the product invoice alone (double-counting). I also found a second, unrelated but adjacent bug while tracing the money: the product-invoice payment step posted the *whole-cart* `paid`/`net` figure against just the product invoice, with no server-side cap on overpaying an invoice (`InvoiceService.AddPaymentAsync` has no such check) — meaning any mixed cart (products + a class item) would already overpay/misrecord the product invoice today, independent of discounts.

**Fix applied** (`SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/pos.astro`):
- Added proportional apportionment: each group's (`nonClassItems`, `collectItems`) share of the total discount = `discAmount × (groupSubtotal / wholeCartSubtotal)`, matching the same principle as the Collect-modal fix.
- `collectItems` loop now sends `discountAmount` (each item's own slice, split further by relative size within the group) and a reduced `amount` to `/collect-payment`, with a `notes` reason (backend requires one for a discount).
- Product invoice creation now sends `discountAmount: prodDiscShare` (its apportioned share only, not the full cart discount).
- Added `prodNet`/`prodPaid` so the product invoice's payment posting is scoped to the product group's own net — preventing the double-count/overpay bug for any mixed cart — while leaving the single-type-cart case byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **Documented, not fixed**: walk-in-checkout items (`walkInItems`) don't receive a discount share — `WalkInCheckoutRequest` only has `ReferralDiscountPct` (a referral-commission percentage, a different concept), so extending it is a separate change. This is a narrower, pre-existing gap that isn't widened by this fix.

**Verified end-to-end on staging** by replaying the exact API call sequence the fixed JS produces for a mixed cart (Grip Socks 200,000 + a collect-payment item at 850,000, flat 300,000 discount): collect invoice came back gross 850,000 / discount 242,857 / net 607,143 / PAID; product invoice came back gross 200,000 / discount 57,143 / net 142,857 / PAID. Discount shares sum to exactly 300,000, and total money collected (750,000) exactly matches subtotal minus discount — no double counting, no overpay.

Built and deployed both images to staging (clean builds, no new compile errors); containers `soulpilates-staging-backend`/`frontend` are up and healthy.
